chat-app-stage-1.title: Direct Messaging
chat-app-stage-1.description: Two browsers talk through one server

nodes.label: Your Browser
nodes.explanation: The client — your web browser running the chat app UI

nodes.label: Server
nodes.explanation: A single server that receives and forwards messages between clients

nodes.label: Friend's Browser
nodes.explanation: Your friend's browser — also a client connected to the same server

chat-app-stage-2.title: Adding Persistence
chat-app-stage-2.description: Messages survive server restarts with a database

nodes.label: Your Browser
nodes.explanation: The client — your web browser running the chat app UI

nodes.label: Server
nodes.explanation: The server that processes messages and stores them in the database

nodes.label: Friend's Browser
nodes.explanation: Your friend's browser — also a client connected to the same server

nodes.label: Database
nodes.explanation: A database that permanently stores all messages on disk — survives server restarts

chat-app-stage-3.title: Real-Time with WebSockets
chat-app-stage-3.description: Persistent connections push messages instantly to all users

nodes.label: User A
nodes.explanation: A connected client with a persistent WebSocket connection to the server

nodes.label: Server
nodes.explanation: The server maintains open WebSocket connections with all active clients

nodes.label: User B
nodes.explanation: Another connected client receiving messages instantly via WebSocket

nodes.label: User C
nodes.explanation: A third client — the server pushes messages to all connected clients simultaneously

nodes.label: Database
nodes.explanation: Still stores all messages permanently — acts as the safety net when clients reconnect
